edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: EPA and DHA lower hepatic VLDL production, shift membrane lipid signaling, and can modestly dampen inflammatory eicosanoid tone. Those mechanisms matter most for Elevated triglycerides when baseline triglycerides are high or the outcome is tightly linked to cardiometabolic inflammation.
edges.summary: Omega-3 in adults with high triglycerides appears tied to lower elevated triglycerides in adults with hypertriglyceridemia mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
